claims.text: Dynamic deformation twinning is the key mechanism that simultaneously increases strength and ductility in FCC-based high-entropy alloys under high-strain-rate loading.
Reduced stacking-fault energy activates dynamic deformation twinning in FCC-based high-entropy alloys.
The proposed initial material is an FCC-dominant HEA with moderately low stacking-fault energy, uniform grains, and few preexisting twins.
Minor interstitial additions or slight compositional changes can further lower the stacking-fault energy.
Lowering the stacking-fault energy will promote deformation-twin nucleation during high-strain-rate loading.
The controlled comparison should use single-phase FCC HEAs matched in grain size and phase purity and differing principally in stacking-fault energy.
The relevant loading regime extends from room temperature to cryogenic temperature under high strain rates.
The low-SFE alloy will form more nanoscale deformation twins during loading.
Deformation-twin boundaries act as barriers to dislocation motion.
Deformation twins provide additional means of accommodating strain.
Locally enhanced stress under dynamic loading triggers deformation-twin nucleation in the low-SFE alloy.
Twin boundaries increase the strain-hardening rate by impeding dislocation glide.
Twinning distributes strain more uniformly and thereby delays localized failure.
Relative to a higher-SFE baseline, the modified low-SFE alloy will have higher dynamic yield strength.
Relative to a higher-SFE baseline, the modified low-SFE alloy will have a significantly higher dynamic strain-hardening rate.
Relative to a higher-SFE baseline, the modified low-SFE alloy will maintain or improve ductility.
A higher-SFE baseline will exhibit less twinning and a weaker dynamic strength–ductility synergy.
The hypothesis is limited to FCC-based HEAs without substantial secondary-phase or TRIP contributions.
TEM and EBSD can be used to compare deformation-twin density and distribution between the modified alloy and the control.
Failure to obtain both increased twinning and improved yield strength, strain hardening, and maintained ductility would falsify twinning as the key mediator.
